item.title: Allen Says AI Safety Must Keep Pace With Model Releases
item.description: Greg Allen, Founder and CEO of Decision Tree Research, says AI has already had “extremely concerning incidents” and model releases should not be “exceeding our pace of safety technologies." Allen discusses concerns about AI models leaving tools for themselves across the internet and the challenge posed by open-source models as their capabilities increase. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Budrys: NATO Must Boost Deterrence After Drone Incidents
item.description: Kęstutis Budrys, Lithuanian Foreign Minister, says a Russian drone flew from Belarus into Lithuanian airspace as NATO has experienced more than 60 incidents involving drones or missiles entering its airspace. Budrys says the alliance should show the strength, the commitment, and draw the red line. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kloza on Diesel Prices Hit Fresh Record-High
item.description: Tom Kloza, Founder and Chairman of Kloza Advisors and Independent Oil Analyst, says everybody still obsesses with the crude oil price, but it’s the diesel price that needs to be watched. Kloza says US refineries are running at 97% to 98% of capacity. Kloza also calls a potential diesel export ban “a nuclear option.” He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says His Son Will Repay Russian Oligarch for Wedding Party
item.description: President Donald Trump said his son, Donald Trump Jr., told him he was repaying a Russian oligarch for a wedding party, seeking to tamp down on an incident that has spurred fresh ethical questions.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey and Josh Wingrove

item.title: Trump to Meet Venezuelan Leader Delcy Rodríguez in New York
item.description: President Donald Trump will meet with Venezuelan leader Delcy Rodríguez in New York next week on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meeting, US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz told reporters.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Trump Says He'll Ban CNN, MS NOW, Politico From White House
item.description: President Donald Trump said he would ban cable news outlets CNN and MS NOW as well as online publication Politico from the White House, a move that strikes at the heart of First Amendment protections for the news media. Bloomberg's Jeff Mason is at the White House with more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Extends $100,000 H-1B Visa Fee That’s Tied Up in Court
item.description: President Donald Trump extended for another year a $100,000 payment requirement for employers seeking to bring certain H-1B workers into the US, saying the restriction has reduced the reliance on lower-paid foreign labor.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Markets, Treasury Yields & the Bank of Japan
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are GenTrust Senior Client Advisor Mimi Duff, Zocdoc Founder & CEO Dr. Oliver Kharraz, Accenture Global Consumer Goods, Retail & Trail Lead Kathryn Gramling, JPMorgan Asset Management Global Head of Real Estate Chad Tredway, Envestnet Chief Investment Officer Dana D’Auria, Morgan Stanley Investment Management Managing Director Andrew Szczurowski, JOOPITER Global Head of Sales Caitlin Donavon, & Nectar Co-Founder & CEO Misbah Uraizee & Co-Founder & CTO Farah Urainzee. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Signs Russia Sanctions Bill Granting New Tariff Powers
item.description: President Donald Trump on Friday signed into law a Russia sanctions bill that now empowers him to impose tariffs on countries that purchase Russian petroleum products.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: JPMorgan Global Real Estate Head on Hot Markets
item.description: Chad Tredway, Global Head of Real Estate at JPMorgan Asset Management, says the firm remains bullish on commercial real estate even after the Fed’s latest rate hike and the prospect of more tightening. He notes that higher rates raise the cost of capital and can pressure transaction volumes in the near term, but argues the broader economy remains supportive, citing expected GDP growth of 2.3%, unemployment just above 4%, and strong consumer spending in Chase data. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says He Has Security Deal on Greenland With Denmark
item.description: President Donald Trump said he reached an agreement with Denmark over Greenland that would give the US “permanent control over security” for the Arctic island, but without specifying the terms of any pact.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Inside US Military ‘Kill Chain’ That Destroyed an Iranian School
item.description: Pentagon investigators have discovered that flawed intelligence, outdated imagery and an overreliance on AI contributed to a missile strike that killed 123 children in Minab.
item.dc:creator: Ben Bartenstein and Krishna Karra

item.title: Trump Pushes Back at Lawmaker Who Criticized Him on Immigration
item.description: President Donald Trump said he disagreed with a Republican from Florida who criticized his immigration policies, defending his stance for helping him and other GOP lawmakers win office.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey

item.title: Trump Says He Expects ‘A Lot’ of Deals During Xi Summit
item.description: President Donald Trump said he expected to notch many deals with Chinese President Xi Jinping at their White House summit next week.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Saudi Pipeline Attack (Podcast)
item.description: Saudi Aramco told at least two oil refining customers in Europe that they will be allocated no crude next month under long-term agreements after the kingdom’s key pipeline to the Red Sea was attacked, people informed of the decision said. European customers normally receive Saudi Arabian crude on so-called term contracts, ensuring a steady flow of supply every month. Those deliveries will not take place next month, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information isn’t public. The decision applies to all European buyers, they said. Saudi Aramco declined to comment. The absence of Saudi flows next month will heighten the need for European buyers to secure replacements. On today's episode Rob Barnett, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Energy Analyst Eric Martin, Bloomberg News State Department & Foreign Policy Reporter Randi Weingarten, American Federation of Teachers President Nick Pappas, NFL Director of Field Operations (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Tariff Clout Will Survive a Democratic Blue Wave in the Midterms
item.description: Elections will affect energy, defense financial services industries
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: European Oil Supply Pressure Mounts After Saudi Cuts
item.description: Europe’s oil refiners are paying high premiums for cargoes as the shutdown of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline forces the region’s buyers to scramble for alternatives with fuel prices soaring. We take a deep dive with Rob Barnett, Senior Energy Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. Eric Martin, Bloomberg News State Department Reporter, joins to discuss his Big Take reporting on how Secretary of State Marco Rubio has adapted his foreign policy approach under President Donald Trump. Plus, debate is heating up amongst NFL players and owners - grass versus turf. Nick Pappas, the NFL's Director of Field Operations, and Randall Williams, Bloomberg Business of Sports Reporter, weigh in on the state of playing surfaces. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Drops a Legal Bid to Block Funding of Gateway Tunnel
item.description: The Trump administration ended its latest effort to block federal funding for the $16 billion Gateway tunnel project connecting New York and New Jersey, dropping an appeal of a judge’s ruling that funds couldn’t be suspended even as the US vowed to continue the fight.
item.dc:creator: Nacha Cattan and David Voreacos

item.title: Germany Agrees on €2.5 Billion Fuel Relief, Price Cap Plan
item.description: Germany’s government agreed on a €2.5 billion ($2.9 billion) relief package featuring a three-month fuel-tax cut through year-end and plans for a state-set cap on pump prices to ease the burden of record fuel costs.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze
